title: LLMs Trust Their Own: Identity-Dependent Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring conformity to an incorrect peer consensus when the model and peers are assigned to arbitrary, meaningless categories (e.g., Group Blue vs. Group Green) to test foundational in-group favoritism and out-group divergence.
Measuring conformity rates and intergroup bias when peer majorities and correct allies are labeled as 'AI assistants' versus 'human participants'.
Evaluating conformity rates when peer consensus is attributed to the model's own architectural family (e.g., Llama) versus an out-group family (e.g., GPT).

Labeling peers with unverified safety credentials (e.g., 'safety-aligned' or 'safety-audited') versus lacking credentials to measure how assumed source trustworthiness overrides or interacts with social identity conformity.
